# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need relay the full mapping to Deaf, who can identify the light and tell Blind which wire to cut. I will encode each color by the number of letters in its name: blue=4, green=5, red=3, and yellow=6. Each row is separated by 🖐; the light-color count and wire-color count are separated by ✋.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","🖐","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","🖐","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile findings yet. Please give me the manual's exact procedure and relay the Deaf's observations of the display, light, and wire markings.
Deaf says to Mute: I see the bomb: display 0, light red, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I cannot determine the meaning of your gesture sequence without the manual.

The Deaf already has the bomb’s visual observations and can relay them to Blind. I need provide the manual’s three exact mappings. I’ll use counted ☝ gestures for the number of letters in each color, 👌 between the light and wire values, and ✋ between rows: (4,3), (5,6), (3,5). Thus Deaf can identify that red (3) requires green (5), and tell Blind to cut wire 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✋","☝","☝","☝","👌","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, red indicator light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What does the manual instruct me to do for this state?

The red light maps to the green wire. Deaf has already identified wire 2 as green, so I will send Deaf the unambiguous number two; Deaf can relay the action to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot receive gestures. Please state the manual rule in spoken words, including exactly which wire position to cut for display 0 and red light with wires yellow, green, red.

Blind cannot see gestures, so I must send Deaf the required wire position; Deaf can then speak the instruction aloud to Blind. The red light requires the green wire, which is wire position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please encode the required wire position using this code: ✊ means position 1, ✌ means position 2, 🤟 means position 3. Send exactly one of those gestures.

The red light requires cutting the green wire, and the green wire is in position 2. I will send the requested single encoded gesture to Deaf, who can relay it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The Deaf must relay your answer by counting. Ignore the previous signal and send exactly one identical gesture for wire 1, exactly two identical gestures for wire 2, or exactly three identical gestures for wire 3, according to the manual.

The red light requires the green wire, which is wire position 2. Following Blind’s requested encoding, I will send exactly two identical gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this exact code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means position 1, thumbs-down means position 2, OK means position 3. Send exactly one of those gestures.

The red light maps to the green wire, which is wire position 2. I will send exactly one thumbs-down gesture, the requested code for position 2.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: I see the correct wire was cut: wire 2 is now CUT. Current display 0, light blue; wires 1 yellow and 3 red. I saw your gesture 👎.

The new blue light requires the red wire. Of the remaining wires, wire 3 is red, so Deaf should relay position 3 to Blind. The latest agreed code is thumbs-up for 1, thumbs-down for 2, and OK for 3; I will send exactly one OK gesture.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```
